newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila assesses impact of peso depreciation.
newsitem.headline: Manila assesses impact of peso depreciation.

text.p: A one-peso depreciation of the Philippine currency is projected to increase the country's total debts, foreign and domestic, by six billion pesos, a finance department study said on Sunday.
A depreciation by that amount is estimated to increase by 500 million pesos the country's foreign debt amortisation for this year, according to the study.
Latest official available figures put Philippine foreign debt at $37.7 billion as of last December.
The country's overall indebtedness, to include domestic obligations, amounts to 1.133 trillion pesos, finance officials said.

The peso tumbled 11.5 percent to 29.40 against the dollar on Friday after the Central Bank allowed the currency to trade within a wider band. The sharp fall forced suspension of the currency's trading and dealing is to resume on Monday.
The finance department study was based on the currency depreciating by one peso, or 3.8 percent, against the dollar.
Such a rate of depreciation, it said, would lead to lower interest rates.

"The (Central Bank) will now be able to bring down its overnight rate, which has increased the rate of the bellwether 91-day T-bills to 12.2 percent from an average of 10.5 percent during the first five months of the year," the study said.

A one-peso depreciation will push up inflation by a slight margin of about 0.5 percent, it said. Thus, inflation could rise from the average January-June level of 4.6 percent to about 5.1 percent, it added.
Food inflation could rise to 1.7 percent from the first quarter figure of 1.3 percent while import prices will go up by about 3.8 percent, the study said.
